title: Scenario 2 — Ordinary Sophie: Plans, Half-Intentions, Changed Mind, Missing Detail

events.content: I’ve got too many things in my head. I should probably apply for that course, except I don’t even know if I want it. I keep saying I’ll sort my CV and then I don’t. Mum wants me to call Auntie tomorrow about something to do with the house, but she didn’t say what. I might go running in the morning if I wake up early. Oh and I definitely need to cancel that subscription before they charge me again — I think it renews this week? I don’t know the date. Also there’s a parcel downstairs I’ve ignored for two days.
I can help keep the real obligations separate from the ‘maybe’ pile. If you want, when you know which subscription it is, tell me and I’ll help you make sure it doesn’t slip.

Didn’t run. Obviously. Don’t make that a thing. I remembered the subscription — it’s Notion, no, sorry, it’s that stock-photo thing. Envato maybe? I’ll check later. Auntie called me first so I don’t need to call her now. It was about Grandad’s paperwork. She said she’ll send me a photo.
Here’s the photo of Grandad’s old insurance letter. Mum wanted to know whether you still had the original.

Oh yeah the original is in Dad’s old folder in the loft, I’m almost certain. I can look tonight. Actually no, I’m not going in the loft tonight. Weekend problem. Also I’ve decided not to apply for that course. I was only looking because I felt behind.
What was the thing I actually needed to cancel? I’ve forgotten again. And there was something with Auntie, but I think she sorted it?

Found it: Freepik annual thing, renews Saturday. Cancel Friday morning please — not today because I still need it for a job. And the Auntie thing isn’t sorted exactly; she wants to know if I have the original, but I’m checking the loft Saturday.
Wait, don’t cancel Freepik yet. The client hasn’t approved the graphics. Push that until tomorrow afternoon if I haven’t told you otherwise.
Client approved. I cancelled Freepik myself. Also found Grandad’s original letter in the loft and sent Auntie a photo. That whole thing can die now.
